newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The truth commission hearing of amnesty applications by South African Communist Party (SACP) leader Chris Hani's killers Janusz Walus and Clive Derby Lewis was told on Monday that statements by the applicants while in detention contradicted the case they were making to be allowed to go free.
- A fundamental review of the system whereby oil companies and/or Mossgas are subsidised by the state has been recommended by the auditor-general.

- Samancor's attributable profit dived 40 percent to 409 million rand in the year to June after low prices for its products, cost-raising production glitches and continued losses from Columbus Stainless, the group said on Monday.

- The greater Johannesburg metropolitan council was experiencing "a bit of a tight cash-flow situation" and had entered into credit negotiations with larger creditors like Eskom and the Rand Water Board, western council CEO Geoff O'Connell said on Monday.
BUSINESS REPORT

- South Africa's oil companies might owe Mossgas, and indirectly South Africa's motorists, hundreds of millions of rands, according to Wally van Heerden, the co-author of a special report on Mossgas released by the auditor-general.
- The government's growth, employment and redistribution (Gear) strategy would eventually result in job creation, Mario Ramos, the director-general of finance, said on Monday.

- Samancor, the steel and ferroalloys division of Billiton, said on Monday it was hit by poor commodity prices and technical problems in the year to June 30, with earnings a share slumping almost 40 percent.

- Employers and governments throughout the South African Development Community (SADC) would be called on to explain massive wage discrepancies and conditions of employment throughout the region, the South African Clothing and Textile Worker's Union (Sactwu) said on Monday.
SAKE BEELD
- Department heads who spend more than their budgets allow and who cannot justify such expenditures will be clamped down on, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Monday.
- Auditor-General Henri Kluever strongly rejected allegations that he knowingly withheld sensitive information about South Africa's oil industry from parliament.
- Poor market conditions, higher production costs and Columbus losses of 57,7 million rand resulted in a poor year for Samancor.
- The Frame group, South Africa's biggest textile manufacturer, showed better results for the year to end June, despite the decline in consumer spending which affected most retail dealers.
THE STAR
- Government departments in greater Johannesburg coughed up 4,8 million rand on Monday ahead of threatened electricity cutoffs to consumers 60 days or more in arrears.

- Legal argument about the admissibility of statements made to police by Clive Derby-Lewis and Janusz Walus dominated the first day of their amnesty hearing for the murder of South African Communist Party leader Chris Hani.

- A woman who admitted to killing her ex-husband's lover has been acquitted of the murder charge, of charges relating to the theft of the murder weapon, and the unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition.
- Thousands of weapons and millions of rounds of ammunition have been destroyed during a joint Mozambique-South Africa police operation in Mozambique.
